scope: Single FCFS server, one model on one GPU, request-level prefill only. Decode, prefix caching, continuous batching, chunked prefill and the scheduler of a real engine are out of scope.
limits: Prefill only on one GPU with a single FCFS queue; a real engine interleaves decode, shares steps and reorders.

Five rounds per (length, chunk); the percentile bootstrap of a median of five values is coarse and tends to undercover. Each round recaptures the graph, and the shortest steps are bimodal between captures.
Prompts under 256 tokens are represented by the 256-token step until shorter steps are measured; prompts over 8192 tokens by the 8192-token step.
Service time is deterministic given the length; replay-to-replay variation inside a capture is not simulated.
Lengths between measured points are interpolated; token counts come from other models' tokenizers.
Dilation keeps the shape of a trace, including idle spans, so rho is a whole-window mean and a window can spend long periods above capacity at a moderate rho; requests are never dropped or timed out.
BurstGPT timestamps have one-second resolution, so ties become simultaneous arrivals (see the jitter sensitivity).

The ten windows are nested (1 h and 24 h inside a week, busiest day inside 61 days) and come from five traces, so the bootstrap over windows is not over independent units; a cluster bootstrap over traces is reported as well.
One board model (stock RTX 3090) and three models; another GPU or engine can change the step latencies.
sign_convention: gain_pct = 100 * (default - variant) / default; positive means the variant is faster

config.prompt_below_lowest_knot: represented by the lowest measured step
config.prompt_above_highest_knot: represented by the highest measured step

elasticity.definition: arc elasticity of the metric when every service time is scaled by 0.99 on fixed arrivals; pk_point = 2 + rho/(1-rho), pk_arc_1pct = the exact P-K value of that step
elasticity.table_vs_uniform_note: cells.<label>.<session>.<tw>.<rho>.trace.elasticity.table_wait_mean is the table's own arc elasticity; it is null when the table changes the mean service time by less than 0.05%

sensitivity_static_batching.policy: A padded batch-4 step runs when at least four requests of the oldest request's length bucket are waiting (padded length at most 2048 tokens, so at most 8192 tokens per step); otherwise the oldest request runs alone at batch 1. Batches of two or three have no measured shape and padding them to batch 4 costs more than serving them singly, so they are not used. Arrivals pinned so that the default's realized busy fraction is rho.
